title: Emit JSON with the right tool: python for arbitrary text, bounded escaping for fixed small fields, and stdout-only
summary: JSON built by string concatenation corrupts the moment a value holds a quote, a backslash, a newline or non-ASCII text. For real serialization, hand raw arguments to a Python heredoc that does genuine json.dumps. Reserve hand-rolled bash escaping for tiny, known-safe fixed structures, and escape in the order backslash first, then quote, then the control characters. Keep all JSON on stdout and diagnostics on stderr.
technique: The dominant safe path is `python3 - "$a" "$b" ... <<'PY'` building a dict and printing json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":")) for deterministic compact output. The bounded bash-only escape helper first doubles backslashes, then backslash-escapes double quotes, then folds newline/carriage/tab to C escapes.
evidence_note: bin/queue-vcs-probe:195-204 builds a JSON probe via a python heredoc with sort_keys/separators. queuebash.sh:6-13 `_queuebash_direct_execution_json_escape_early` escapes in the `\ -> " -> controls` order for a small known-safe string; docs/QUEUE_COMMAND_CONTRACT.md states JSON output is parseable on stdout only with diagnostics to stderr.
invariants: Do not build a JSON document from unknown input by string concatenation; use a real serializer.
For pure-bash escaping, substitute backslash first, then double quote, then control characters, and only for a bounded, single-type field you control.
Emit exactly one JSON document on stdout in JSON mode; keep human warnings and logs off stdout (stderr/audit).
Mark documented envelopes with a versioned schema field so a change is a new schema, not a silent reshape.
